grades.quote: Attempting to fetch an instruction from a page that does not have execute permissions raises a fetch page-fault exception.
grades.reason: Gives the R/W/X permission encoding table, the page faults raised for fetch, load and store/AMO violations, and the U bit with SUM rules for user-mode and supervisor access. This answers every part of the query.

grades.quote: PTE_R controls whether instructions are allowed to read to the page. PTE_W controls whether instructions are allowed to write to the page. PTE_X controls whether the CPU may interpret the content of the page as instructions and execute them. PTE_U controls whether instructions in user mode are allowed to access the page; if PTE_U is not set, the PTE can be used only in supervisor mode.
grades.reason: Explains that the RISC-V PTE flag bits PTE_R, PTE_W, PTE_X and PTE_U control read, write, execute and user-mode access. It is less detailed on faults but covers all the permissions asked about.

grades.quote: The permission bits, R, W, and X, indicate whether the page is readable, writable, and executable, respectively.
grades.reason: Introduces the Sv32 PTE and its R, W, X permission bits, including the pointer-versus-leaf distinction and the rule that writable pages must be readable. The encoding table content is missing, and the passage does not discuss the U bit or user access.

grades.quote: When SUM=0, S-mode memory accesses to pages that are accessible by U-mode (U=1 in Figure 67) will fault.
grades.reason: Covers how the sstatus MXR and SUM bits modify the R and U page permissions. It addresses supervisor access to user pages and says S-mode can never execute from user pages. It does not describe the basic PTE R/W/X/U permission semantics.
